ku_abstract.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2 [math.PR], 11 Sep 2024 (last update 12 Sep 2024), p. 1 (abstract)
ku_abstract.text: The well-known Isothermal Theorem was introduced in a Nature Communications article in 2005 and has since contributed to the creation of the rich field of evolutionary graph theory. ... Unfortunately, the Isothermal Theorem has never been proven completely. The main argument, that the projection of the process on the graph dynamics onto a one-dimensional process is a Birth-and-Death-Process, is not true in general, as the projection does not need to be Markovian. The aim of this paper is to present a more general version of the Isothermal Theorem using martingale techniques and a generalised framework using matrix notation.

ku_gap.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2, p. 4 (Section 1.2) and p. 7 (Section 2.2)
ku_gap.text: In [LHN05], the authors claim that under some conditions on the graph and the weights, this process has the same fixation probabilities as the Moran process ... The proof uses a projection onto a simpler process (M_k)_k. ... They then use results from Birth-and-Death-Processes for the computation of the fixation probability. Unfortunately, this method fails, as the projection of a Markov Chain is not necessarily Markov, unless under lumpability ... This shortcoming has not been noticed in the literature so far, not even in the recent review paper [DM21]. Therefore, the isothermal theorem remains unproven till today. [p. 4] ... Nevertheless, it does not follow that (M_k)_k is a Markov Chain in general, since usually E[M_{k+1} | F_k] != E[M_{k+1} | M_k]. [p. 7]

ku_thm31.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2, pp. 5-6 (Definition 2.1), p. 9 (Theorem 3.1 and proof)
ku_thm31.text: Definition 2.1: ... Let pi be [the] unique strictly positive and normed left-eigenvector [of W] (pi W = pi). We call pi selection policy. ... a vertex v is selected for procreation under selection policy pi and fitness r with probability r pi(v)/(1+(r-1) zeta_k) if v is labelled with 1 (mutant), pi(v)/(1+(r-1) zeta_k) if v is labelled with 0 (wildtype). Independently, another vertex v' is chosen randomly according to the probability measure W(v, .). [p. 6] ... Theorem 3.1: Let <(X_k)_k, W, pi, r> be a micSMP, as in Definition 2.1. Then, for any initial distribution alpha concentrated on X_j, P(T_fix < infinity | X_0 ~ alpha) = i/n (r = 1), (1 - 1/r^i)/(1 - 1/r^n) (r != 1). Proof. We construct a particular martingale and use the Optional Stopping Theorem. ... for all configurations x in X \ {X_0 u X_n}: p^-(x)/p^+(x) = 1/r ... N_k := r^{-M_k} ... is indeed a F-martingale ... [p. 9-10]. (Typos of the source in the displayed formulas - 'r = 0' on p. 2, 'r^i' for 'r^{-i}' on p. 3, X_j vs i, the missing exponent n on p. 7 - are not copied.)

ku_thm32.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2, p. 10 (Theorem 3.2)
ku_thm32.text: Theorem 3.2: In a micSMP <(X_k)_k, W, mu, r> with arbitrary selection policy mu, we have for any configuration x ... Further, p^-/p^+ is a constant function if and only if mu = pi, where pi W = pi. In that case p^-_mu(x)/p^+_mu(x) = 1/r.

ku_iso.source: P. Keller, M. Ugurlu, arXiv:2403.12598v2, p. 7 (Section 2.3)
ku_iso.text: The isothermal property indeed just says that for any vertex of the graph the sum of incoming weights is equal to the sum of outgoing weights. In matrix notation, this is just W 1^T = W^T 1^T = 1^T. The last equality holds because of the assumed stochasticity of W. From this, W is isothermal if and only if W is bistochastic, and the invariant measure of W, fulfilling pi W = pi, must be uniform.

pattni_title.source: K. Pattni, M. Broom, J. Rychtar, L. J. Silvers, arXiv:1505.06021v1 [q-bio.PE], 22 May 2015, p. 1
pattni_title.text: Evolutionary graph theory revisited: general dynamics and the Moran process. Karan Pattni, Mark Broom, Jan Rychtar and Lara J. Silvers. ... In this paper we revisit the original paper on evolutionary graph theory in light of these extensions to consider these developments in an integrated way. In particular we find general criteria for when an evolutionary graph with general weights satisfies the Moran probability for the set of six common evolutionary dynamics.

pattni_lemma1.source: K. Pattni et al., arXiv:1505.06021v1, p. 11 (Appendix A.2) and pp. 11-12 (proof)
pattni_lemma1.text: The key Lemma 1 stated below is used in the proofs of all propositions and it relies heavily on the notion of forward bias of state S which is then given by the ratio of the probabilities of a forward transition to a backward transition from S. ... P+_S = sum_{n not in S} P_{S,S u {n}} and P-_S = sum_{n in S} P_{S,S\{n}}. Lemma 1 (Constant Forward Bias). Let E be an evolutionary process on states S subset {1,...,N} with transition probabilities P_{S,S'} that satisfy: P_{S,S'} > 0 only if S and S' differ in at most one element; for every S != empty, {1,...,N}, there are S+ and S- such that |S+| = |S|+1 and |S-| = |S|-1 and P_{S,S+} > 0, P_{S,S-} > 0. Then, the following are equivalent: a) There is a constant c > 0 such that for all S, rho^A_S = (1 - c^{-|S|})/(1 - c^{-N}) if c != 1, |S|/N if c = 1. b) E has constant forward bias, that is, there is a constant d such that for all S, P+_S / P-_S = d. Moreover, if either (a) or (b) hold, then c = d. [p. 11] ... Proof of (b) => (a): The state transition matrix S can be scaled to give S' ... P'_{S,S'} = P_{S,S'}/(1 - P_{S,S}) = P_{S,S'}/(P+_S + P-_S) where S is a non-absorbing state. The fixation probability rho^A_S will be the same whether S' or S is used. ... [the lumped chain over the partition by |S|] ... P_{i,j}(S) = 0 (j != i +- 1), 1/(d+1) (j = i-1), d/(d+1) (j = i+1) ... satisfies the necessary and sufficient condition for the Markov chain with state transition matrix S' to be lumpable with respect to the partition (Theorem 6.3.2 page 124, [Kemeny-Snell]). [p. 12]
